title: Ribo-Seq/ART-Seq/GTI-Seq
scope: Illumina explanatory schematic and explicitly supported method variants. The PNG depicts one unbranched route from ribosome-bound RNA through RNase digestion, two separately captioned RNA extractions with intervening rRNA depletion, reverse transcription and cDNA. Sequencing is a catalogue-supported downstream readout. Ribo-Seq/ART-Seq are catalogue aliases at this schematic level, not a claim of identity among all implementations or of exact reproduction of the 2009 experiment. Separate text-only GTI-Seq records retain the LTM initiation-selection distinction and a broad footprint-readout interface from the supplied TISdb paper; they are not additional branches drawn in the PNG. No historical-development or interchangeability edge is inferred.

states.label: Ribosome-bound RNA
features: Main-workflow input: purple RNA adjacent to blue ribosome components above the caption Ribosome.

Far-left overview: a blue ribosome with a long RNA strand highlighted in yellow; caption reads Ribo-Seq: Ribosome profiling, Global translation initiation sequencing (GTI-Seq). This is a descriptive overview, not a transfer arrow or an extra assembly operation.
There is one left-to-right main route, with no retained sample branches, end-group annotations or molecular legend.

states.label: cDNA corresponding to recovered footprint RNA
features: The final product is one black strand labelled cDNA.
Under Reverse transcription a parallel purple/black intermediate precedes the final black strand; RNA-template removal chemistry is not labelled.
This is the schematic cDNA endpoint; the figure does not specify all features required for an instrument-ready library.
The molecular carrier of footprint sequence information is DNA copied from recovered RNA, not the original ribosome or a synthesized protein.

evidence.locator: Arrow from second "RNA extraction" to "Reverse transcription" (parallel purple and black strands), then arrow to single black "cDNA" strand
Full text [b00008], Quantifying RNA with deep sequencing
evidence.quote: (i) robustly generate ribosome-protected mRNA fragments (“footprints”) whose sequences indicate the position of active ribosomes; (ii) convert these RNA footprints into a library of DNA molecules in a form that is suitable for deep sequencing with minimal distortion; and (iii) measure the abundance of different footprints in this library by means of deep sequencing.

states.label: Sequences representing ribosome-associated RNA fragments
features: Sequencing is specified in the catalogue text after the depicted cDNA endpoint; it is not drawn in the PNG.
The cDNA inserts represent recovered ribosome-protected RNA fragments, not full-length transcript molecules.
Mapping footprint sequences to transcripts reports occupied regions; aggregate footprints can reveal the translated reading frame. A single footprint gives imperfect statistical positional evidence.

Counts measure footprint abundance in the library. Estimates of protein synthesis from ribosome density depend on translation-speed assumptions; these are not direct measurements of elongation kinetics.
Translation-efficiency comparisons additionally require mRNA abundance, a separate measurement outside this drawing.

states.label: GTI-Seq footprint reads supporting translation-initiation-site positions
features: Read sequences represent LTM-associated ribosome footprints, enriched near initiation sites.
Mapped footprints support identification of canonical and alternative TIS positions; the TISdb paper does not provide the intervening RNA recovery and library chemistry.
For the GTI-Seq datasets described by TISdb, read density is not a translation-initiation-rate measurement. Low-abundance transcripts or weak initiation sites may escape detection.

operations.label: RNase digestion
operations.description: Digest exposed regions of ribosome-bound RNA, leaving the protected RNA associated with the ribosome. The yellow icon accompanies this reaction and is not an independently retained material.
operations.mechanism: Nuclease digestion of RNA outside ribosome protection.
operations.information_effect: Ribosome protection selects fragments of the associated mRNA. Their sequences carry information about regions occupied by ribosomes; this is a footprint measurement rather than sequencing of the ribosome protein.

operations.label: RNA extraction

operations.label: rRNA depletion
operations.description: Reduce rRNA in the extracted RNA mixture while retaining the purple footprint RNA. The faded rRNA icon indicates depletion without specifying the removal mechanism or completeness. This is a catalogue-schematic operation. The 2009 paper reports rRNA contamination and proposes subtractive hybridization; it does not establish that this particular depletion was performed in that study.
operations.information_effect: Reduce ribosomal-RNA contamination in the material carried toward cDNA.

evidence.quote: 7.0 million (16%) of sequencing reads aligned to CDSs, whereas most of the remainder were derived from ribosomal RNA (rRNA) (table S1). Because most contaminating rRNA is derived from a few specific sites, it should be straight-forward to remove them by means of subtractive hybridization before sequencing.
evidence.rationale: This describes residual rRNA in the reported experiment and proposes subtraction. It does not document execution of the schematic depletion stage.

operations.label: RNA extraction
operations.description: Recover the RNA fraction following rRNA depletion. This is the second extraction caption in the drawing, whose product is the isolated short purple strand.
operations.information_effect: Carry the recovered footprint RNA forward as the reverse-transcription substrate.

evidence.locator: Arrow from "rRNA depletion" to second "RNA extraction"; only a short horizontal purple strand remains

operations.label: Reverse transcription
operations.description: Copy the recovered RNA into cDNA. The depicted purple/black parallel strands precede an arrow to a single black cDNA strand. This operation record includes that schematic endpoint, without inventing an enzyme or a separate unlabelled template-removal procedure.
operations.mechanism: RNA-templated cDNA synthesis; conversion from the depicted two-strand intermediate to the final cDNA is chemically unspecified.
operations.information_effect: The cDNA is a DNA copy of the protected RNA, rather than a protein readout or a retained RNA–ribosome complex.

operations.label: Deep sequencing of cDNA (catalogue readout; not drawn)
operations.description: Read the DNA representation of recovered ribosome-associated RNA. This is a text-supported readout interface, not a reconstruction of unshown adapter addition, amplification or instrument chemistry.
operations.information_effect: DNA sequence reads preserve footprint identity and, after mapping, location on transcripts. method_scopes.rationale: Resolved for the Illumina schematic and catalogue description: protected mRNA is recovered, rRNA depleted, and RNA converted to a cDNA representation for sequencing. Ingolia et al. 2009 supports the footprint/DNA-library principle and readout, not an exact match to every catalogue cleanup step. In particular, it proposes rRNA subtraction rather than reporting the drawn depletion as executed. The Ribosome icon is starting material, and the far-left icon is an overview.

method_scopes.rationale: The GTI-Seq-specific distinction is resolved: the supplied TISdb full text describes LTM-enriched initiating ribosomes and footprint reads that localize TIS positions. These two operations are a separate text-supported aggregate, not a second branch visible in the PNG. Applicability of the entire drawn cleanup sequence, especially rRNA depletion and the second RNA extraction, to a particular GTI-Seq implementation is unresolved because the database paper does not specify that preparation. The catalogue harringtonine sentence describes a different initiation-profiling approach discussed separately by TISdb; it is not substituted for LTM.
